- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

=== .gitignore ===
*/fixtures/*.o
*/fixtures/*.elf
=== README.md ===
# Engine registration contract

andesim is a commercial product. An engine is "supported" only when it is
REGISTERED: it has its own CSR report and its own passing test set. A
rebuild of the same core with a different config is a NEW registration --
the identity is the engine name plus a hash of its build `config.inc`, so
stale artifacts can never be silently reused.

## What a new engine registration needs (inputs)

1. The built engine binary (`$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine>`) and its build
   config (`$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc`).
2. The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family.
3. The QEMU pairing for the oracle/fast leg (`-cpu` name, vlen, march).

## What must be produced (artifacts, per engine build)

```
tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/
├── engine.env               # engine name, config hash, QEMU pairing, vlen, priv levels
├── rtl_params.json          # resolved RTL params for the shared generator's
│                            #   EXCL_SIDEFX-only RTL fallback (provenance in "notes")
├── csr_manifest.csv         # machine-readable: one row per spec CSR
│                            #   GENERATED: python3 tests/engines/gen_manifest.py <regdir>
│                            #   (ONE shared generator; it runs the probe itself)
├── csr_restore_table.md     # human-readable: restored? condition met / unmet / why
│                            #   GENERATED from the manifest (render_restore_table.py);
│                            #   test_restore_table.sh fails on drift -- never hand-edit
└── registration_report.md   # the CSR report -- guides agents to generate tests
```

`csr_manifest.csv` columns (one row per spec-inventory CSR, all ~232):

| column | meaning | source |
|---|---|---|
| addr, name, access | identity + access mode | spec inventory |
| exists_cond | existence condition, spec language | SPA IM Requirement / Table 13 |
| implemented | does THIS engine have it | MEASURED by the probe (gen_manifest.py auto-runs probe_engine.sh); RTL `existent_csr` only for the EXCL_SIDEFX CSRs the probe skips |
| transported | restored + drained by the hybrid handoff | engine `--describe andes_csrs` / caps |
| gate_or_disposition | why (gate name, or EXCL_* reason) | caps map / coverage matrix |
| verify | compared / excluded (+ why) | driver `state_diff.cpp` |
| reset_value | the engine's real reset value | MEASURED by the probe on the reset hart, never the spec column |
| safe_write | mask or skip for write-survival fixtures | reviewed policy |

`registration_report.md` must contain:
1. the three-way translation table for every gated CSR (spec condition <->
   RTL `existent_csr` term <-> config.inc knobs) -- see the
   csr-transport-bringup skill's `three-way-audit.md` for the method;
2. the empirical validation evidence: a cold-cache hybrid `--verify` run on
   this engine (the fresh baseline capture sweeps every claimed CSR on the
   RTL -- the over-claim proof) with the PASS line and compared-field count;
3. the under-claim check result: every engine-existent transportable CSR is
   claimed or carries a named EXCL_* reason -- gaps listed, or "none";
4. a DISCREPANCIES section: every spec-vs-engine disagreement, classified
   (interpretation-unresolved / QEMU-model artifact / suspected RTL bug /
   suspected spec error -- the skill's three-way-audit.md defines the
   classes and triangulation method), each with verbatim quoted evidence
   (file:line, PDF page) and its disposition. Transport always follows the
   ENGINE so nothing faults, but a suspected RTL or spec bug must be
   escalated to its owners, never silently absorbed into the caps table.
   A validation result is only trustworthy if this section exists -- even
   when it says "none";
5. test-generation guidance: which CSRs get write-survival fixtures, their
   safe-write masks, the write-ordering constraints (mstatus.FS/VS first,
   mcounterwen before counter masks, msp_bound/base before mhsp_ctl, vsetvl
   rules), and the exact run commands for this engine.

## The invariant: every supported CSR is tested or named-excluded

Registration passes only if every `implemented` CSR falls in exactly one bucket,
each machine-checked:
- **transported + tested** -- restored at resume, drained, `--verify`-compared,
  AND has its own per-CSR test (write-survival, read-back, or a named covered/
  verify-only disposition).
- **named-excluded** -- not transported, with a named reason
  (`CONST_RO`, `EXCL_*`, or a `gate=off` for a feature this config lacks).

Neither-bucket = silent state loss = FAIL. Transported without a test = FAIL.
See `docs/engine_registration_completeness_ROADMAP.md`.

## What must pass (checks, before "supported")

1. vsim caps unit test modeling this engine's config shape
   (`tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` helper, e.g. `premium()`/`advanced()`).
2. Caps parity guard (`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_caps_parity.sh` --
   picks up every built engine automatically).
3. Cold-cache hybrid `--verify` PASS on this engine, both trigger modes.
4. Under-claim HARD gate (`check_completeness.py` via
   `test_registration_completeness.sh`): any `implemented in {yes,partial}` &
   `transported=no` row whose disposition is not `CONST_RO`/`EXCL_*` FAILS.
   This is the implemented->transported direction as a failing test, not a note.
5. Test-coverage HARD gate (`check_test_coverage.py` via
   `test_registration_coverage.sh`): every transported RW CSR must have a
   `safe_write_policy.csv` disposition in {write, readback, covered,
   verify-only}; the retired `skip` (or a missing row) FAILS. This is the
   transported->tested direction.
6. Coverage guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`: spec == matrix == ABI).
7. The engine's generated fixtures pass (`gen_fixtures.py` x
   `safe_write_policy.csv` -> `fixtures/csr_survival_gen.S` [write] +
   `fixtures/csr_readback_gen.S` [read-back], regenerated + rebuilt +
   `--verify`-run by `test_registration_fixtures.sh`).

Read-back vs write: control CSRs unsafe to blind-write (mcache_ctl, mxstatus, ...)
get a read-back fixture -- stash the live value pre-ROI, prove it survived resume
in-ROI, no destructive write. It is a SEPARATE ELF from the write fixture (a
`csrw mcounterinten` in the same lengthened ROI perturbs the run). A CSR whose
drained value diverges vsim-vs-QEMU (e.g. tdata1) is verify-only, not read-back.

The standing enforcement (wired into `scripts/test_all.sh` via the
`tests/engines/test_*.sh` glob):
- `test_registration_guard.sh` -- every BUILT engine has a hash-matched,
  complete registration; unregistered or stale-config engines FAIL.
- `test_registration_completeness.sh` -- check 4, on every registered manifest.
- `test_registration_coverage.sh` -- check 5, on every registered manifest.
- `test_registration_fixtures.sh` -- check 7, re-proven on every suite run
  for every registration whose engine is built here.

## Removing an engine (deregistration)

Dropping support is a deliberate, single commit -- the reverse of
registration -- so "we no longer support X" is as traceable as "we support
X". Removing only the build (e.g. trimming vsim's `config.yaml` locally)
does NOT deregister: the registration dir stays and the suite simply skips
the engine (the parity guard and matrix runner skip engines that are not
built -- that is the "temporarily not built" state, not removal).

Checklist for real removal (one commit per registration):

1. Delete `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/` (the manifest, report,
   and generated fixtures go together -- git history keeps the report
   retrievable for commercial traceability, so never rewrite it, just
   delete).
2. Remove the engine from the vsim build (`config.yaml` in the vsim repo)
   and delete its stale binaries/build dir; also clear its baseline caches
   (`~/.cache/andesim/sim_<engine>-*`, harmless but confusing to keep).
3. Remove or re-point suite entries pinned to this engine
   (`scripts/run_e2e.sh` -- e.g. the S/U privilege fixtures name their
   engine explicitly; they need a replacement S/U-capable engine or must be
   marked skipped, never silently dropped).
4. Remove engine-specific QEMU-pairing entries in the driver's engine
   registry, and sweep the docs (`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` examples, CLAUDE.md)

5. KEEP the spec-knowledge tests: the vsim caps gate-rule tests (e.g. the

"""Shared helpers for the engine-registration tooling.

Single home for the CSR range grammar (name rows like 'mhpmevent3~6', addr
rows like '0xBD0~0xBFF' / '0x3A4~3AF'), the safe_write_policy.csv load, and
manifest discovery -- so the generator, the checkers, and the probe cannot
drift apart on these conventions.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import os
import re

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

_NAME_RANGE = re.compile(r"^(.*?)(\d+)~(\d+)$")
_ADDR = re.compile(r"^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+$")
_ADDR_RANGE = re.compile(r"^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)~(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$")


def expand_names(name: str) -> list[str]:
    """inventory range row ('mhpmevent3~6') -> individual CSR names."""
    m = _NAME_RANGE.match(name)
    if not m:
        return [name]
    stem, lo, hi = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
    return [f"{stem}{i}" for i in range(lo, hi + 1)]


def polname(name: str) -> str:
    """Manifest CSR name -> safe_write_policy key (a range row collapses to
    its low member)."""
    m = _NAME_RANGE.match(name)
    return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}" if m else name


def expand_addrs(s: str) -> list[int]:
    """inventory addr string -> list of ints; the range's high half may be
    truncated to a shared-prefix suffix ('0x3A4~3AF'). Unparseable -> []."""
    s = s.strip()
    if _ADDR.match(s):
        return [int(s, 16)]
    m = _ADDR_RANGE.match(s)
    if not m:
        return []
    lo_s, hi_s = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    lo = int(lo_s, 16)
    hi = int(lo_s[: len(lo_s) - len(hi_s)] + hi_s, 16) \
        if len(hi_s) < len(lo_s) else int(hi_s, 16)
    return list(range(lo, hi + 1))


def load_policy() -> dict[str, dict]:
    """safe_write_policy.csv rows keyed by CSR name."""
    with open(os.path.join(HERE, "safe_write_policy.csv"), newline="") as f:
        return {r["name"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(f)}


def manifest_paths(argv: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """CLI manifest args, or every registered manifest under tests/engines/."""
    return argv[1:] or sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(HERE, "*", "csr_manifest.csv")))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Engine registration: CSR manifest + both-direction completeness check.

ONE shared generator for every registered engine (was: a per-engine copy in
each registration dir). The engine is selected by the regdir argument:
`engine.env` names the binary, `rtl_params.json` carries the build's resolved
RTL parameters (and the few wire overrides a regex cannot resolve).

Sources (the three-way audit):
  SPEC : AndeStar V5 SPA Table 13 + per-CSR IM Requirement (curated below)
  CONFIG: build config.inc (parsed) + resolved RTL localparams
          (regdir/rtl_params.json -- provenance in its "notes")
  RTL  : existent_csr equation from the BUILD kv_csr_dec.v, machine-evaluated

Empirical ("measure, don't model"):
  - implemented set + reset values: the sim_<engine> --probe measurement on
    the freshly reset halted hart. The generator runs probe_engine.sh itself;
    ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV only reuses an existing capture. The RTL equation is a
    fallback ONLY for the read-side-effect CSRs the probe must skip.
  - transported (claimed) set: sim_<engine> --describe andes_csrs
    (crosschecked against scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py -- parity)

Usage:
  gen_manifest.py <regdir>       # e.g. tests/engines/ax45mpv_premium-5bea8bdc
"""
import csv, re, subprocess, sys, os, json, tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
AND = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))            # repo root
OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
assert OUT and os.path.isdir(OUT), "usage: gen_manifest.py <regdir>"


def _cfg(key):
    """config.env value, environment override first."""
    if os.getenv(key):
        return os.getenv(key)
    with open(os.path.join(AND, "config.env")) as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.startswith(key + "="):
                return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip('"')
    raise KeyError(key)


ENV = {}
with open(os.path.join(OUT, "engine.env")) as f:
    for line in f:
        if "=" in line and not line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            ENV[k.strip()] = v.strip()
ENGINE = ENV["ENGINE"]
VSIM_BIN_DIR = _cfg("VSIM_BIN_DIR")
SIM = os.path.join(VSIM_BIN_DIR, "sim_" + ENGINE)
DEC = os.path.join(VSIM_BIN_DIR, "V" + ENGINE,
                   "andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v")

# Measure, don't model: the probe (a checked read of every inventory CSR on
# the halted reset hart) is THE source for implemented + reset values. With no
# ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV the generator runs probe_engine.sh itself; the env var
# only lets you reuse a capture. The RTL equation below is a FALLBACK for the
# read-side-effect (EXCL_SIDEFX) CSRs the probe must skip -- any other CSR
# missing from the probe is an error, never a silent model.
_probe = {}

# "params": resolved config/localparam values (provenance in "notes");
# "wire_overrides": wires the resolver below cannot read from the decoder
# source (generate-block assignments), pinned to their built value.

def verilog_to_py(expr: str) -> str:
    expr = re.sub(r"12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)", lambda m: "0x" + m.group(1), expr)

# the generation writes hex literals instead).

      re.findall(r"localparam\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*;", src)}

# param/localparam/override is looked up as `wire <name> = <expr>;` in the
# decoder source and resolved recursively. Handles both decoder generations
# (premium: s0..s8 helper wires + CSR12_* localparams; advanced: named wires
# + hex literals). csr_addr-dependent wires re-evaluate per address.
_IDENT = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z_]\w*\b")

    for name in _IDENT.findall(expr):
        if name in P or name in W or name in LP or name == "csr_addr":

        if name in _WIRE_EXPRS or name in stack:

        _collect(wexpr, stack + (name,))
